narrative.overview:
The site is a children's pop-up book lying open on a cobalt table. Every chapter is a full-bleed spread of flat gouache colour with a fold down the middle; everything that stands on it is die-cut card, coloured on the face, showing a white core at every cut edge, casting a soft shadow onto the page. The hero is a real WebGL pop-up book whose right page springs a cut-paper grass tree up out of the gutter, in the bulldozer's way. Illustrations are cut paper (SVG shapes and extruded 3D cards), never icons pasted on; photos are tipped in as snapshots with tape.

The book is meant to be played with. Things answer a hand: the pull-tab grows the tree, the price flap flips, the height chart stands up and leans from the cursor, snapshots can be picked up, the care wheel spins, map flags fold up. Every movement uses one damped spring that overshoots and settles. Colour is loud and saturated but held in fields: one field per spread, one colour per card. One yellow is kept back for ordering, so the eye always finds the way to buy.

The previous "Flagging Tape and Tree Tags" world (white sand ground, pink tape, hairline panels, Anybody and Lexend) was rejected and nothing visual carries over from it.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed gouache spreads with a gutter fold, on a cobalt table.
Die-cut card everywhere: coloured face, white core rim, soft cast shadow.
Wattle yellow belongs to ordering and nothing else.
Gluten for titles, figures, tabs and the book's own captions; Andika for every sentence a person reads.
Spring overshoot on everything, in a fixed grammar: open, stand, slide, spin, lift, flutter.
Works fully without WebGL and with reduced motion.

rules.name: The Wattle Law Rule
rules.body: Wattle yellow is reserved for ordering controls: the "Add to my order" buttons, the header order pill, the size pull-tab that sets what you add, shelf steppers, chosen day and time chips, the chosen send method, the order progress fill, chat "add" actions, and the label that flies into the order. Nothing decorative, informational or navigational is ever yellow. If it does not build or send an order, it is not yellow.

rules.name: The One Field Rule
rules.body: Each spread is one flat colour field; each card is one flat colour. No gradients between palette colours; texture comes from the shared paper grain, not from colour mixing.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Gluten names, counts and narrates; Andika instructs and explains. Any instruction, answer, form label or paragraph is Andika.

rules.name: The Big Print Rule
rules.body: Body is 1.15rem. Nothing a person must act on sits below 0.95rem.

rules.name: The Spread Rule
rules.body: Every chapter is a full-bleed gouache field spread: one palette colour edge to edge, the shared paper grain over it, a 22px shade at the top where the next page's edge lies, and a 140px gutter fold shading down the centre line. Content sits on two pages either side of the fold (1fr 1fr with a clamp 3-9rem gap; the left page right-aligned, max 36rem) or runs across both pages capped at 82rem. Spreads are padded by the band (clamp 4.5-7.5rem) and the fluid gutter. The sequence is fixed by the story: cobalt hero, sky sizes, paper shelf, cobalt home, earth rescue, gum care, crown visit, earth-deep back cover.

rules.name: The Title Over the Book Rule
rules.body: The hero H1 sits on the cobalt table above the open book's left page, like a title over the book, never on the page. The left page cannot hold a 4rem-plus headline and the size picker at a legible size, so the page carries the lede, head toggle, pull-tab, price flap and order button, and the headline is sized to the table space above it. On phones and narrow aspect ratios (900px or below 23:20) the pop-up takes the top 54svh and the headline and picker sit on a paper panel below it.

rules.name: The Die-Cut Rule
rules.body: Anything cut from card shows its white core and casts a soft shadow. In SVG that is the `#cut` filter; in 3D it is `card()`, a shape extruded to 0.007 card thickness with the face in its colour and the extruded edge in Card Core, casting and receiving shadows. A coloured shape with no core rim is a sticker, not card.

rules.name: The Soft Shadow Rule
rules.body: No zero-blur ledge shadows. Every cast shadow has blur and falls down and away from the light; no hard offset blocks under text, buttons or cards. Pressed impressions into the board are the only zero-blur edges.

rules.name: The Spring Rule
rules.body: One spring for everything: `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)` in CSS, damped springs in JS and WebGL. Exits and page swings use `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`. The grammar is fixed: open (pages and sheets swing on a hinge), stand (cards and chart trees rise from folded flat), slide (tabs, trucks, chips), spin (care wheel, wheel stages), lift (snapshots, flaps, the crane), flutter (paper leaves and the crown in a gust). Headings arrive word by word with a small tilt.

rules.name: The Already There Rule
rules.body: Entrances start from visible: an element waiting for its entrance is offset, folded or tilted, never hidden, so a missed observer never hides content.

rules.name: The Still Book Rule
rules.body: Under reduced motion every state change stays (sizes, prices, steps, stages), and the scroll pin, springs, travel and flutter are dropped; springs jump to their targets and the 3D scene renders only on change.

dos: **Do** make every chapter a full-bleed gouache spread with a gutter fold, in the fixed story order.
**Do** keep wattle yellow (#ffc928) for ordering controls only.
**Do** give every cut shape a Card Core rim and a soft cast shadow: the `#cut` filter in SVG, `card()` in 3D.
**Do** move everything on the spring (cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)) within the open / stand / slide / spin / lift / flutter grammar.
**Do** start entrances from visible: offset, folded or tilted, never at zero opacity.
**Do** set the hero H1 on the cobalt table above the left page, not on the page.
**Do** caption every photo with where it came from.
**Do** keep reduced motion fully working: keep state changes, drop the scroll pin, springs and flutter.
**Do** fall back to the Fremantle photo when WebGL is missing.
donts: **Don't** use wattle yellow for decoration, highlights, navigation, status or headings.
**Don't** use zero-blur ledge shadows or hard offset blocks under text, buttons or cards.
**Don't** draw cut-paper shapes without their white core rim.
**Don't** blend palette colours in gradients; one field per spread, one colour per card.
**Don't** set instructions, answers or labels in Gluten, or anything actionable below 0.95rem.
**Don't** bring back the rejected tape world: no pink tape, white sand ground, hairline panels, Anybody or Lexend.
